answer: New identities sit frozen as tundra: no payout until grafted onto a living orchard, where an established owner stakes a graft bond. The k-th graft on one orchard burns k squared, so a farm hanging n clones off a single tree pays about n cubed over three, and that tree's fruit is split among grafts, diluting every clone. Reaching the zenith tier needs a graft whose two parents come from a disjoint orchard, so a cluster cannot lift itself. Graft bonds stay bound to the tree and cannot be sold, and lineage is public, so pooling buys a longer bill, not more reach.
